nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains small amounts of potassium, iron, and vitamin C depending on ingredients. Primarily contributes flavour, colour, and umami rather than bulk nutrition.

Sauces.purpose: Provides flavour, colour, heat, and umami depth to a wide range of dishes. Each sauce contributes specific qualities: BBQ and hoisin add sweetness and caramelisation; fish and oyster sauces provide salty umami; soy sauces enhance saltiness and colour; tomato sauces add acidity and sweetness; Worcestershire adds tang and depth; Sriracha provides spicy heat and garlic notes. Essential for marinades, stir-fries, condiments, glazes, and finishing touches.
Sauces.usageTips:
usage:

- **Barbecue / BBQ Sauce:** Typically tomato-based with vinegar, sugar, and spices.

Seafood.notes: Seafood encompasses fish and shellfish used across a range of bistro and home recipes. - **Fish Fillets (Fresh):** Choose firm-fleshed white fish like barramundi, snapper, flathead, or blue-eye trevalla for pan-frying and bistro presentations. Pat dry before cooking; do not overcook — flesh should be just opaque. - **King Prawns:** Large prawns used whole or peeled and deveined. Grill, pan-fry, or add to sauces; cook until just pink — 2–3 minutes. Overcooked prawns become rubbery. - **Oysters:** Best served freshly shucked. When used in cooking (e.g., Carpetbag steak), lightly pan-fry or add at the last minute. - **Scallops:** Sear over very high heat, 1–2 minutes each side, to achieve a golden crust without overcooking. - **Seafood Mix:** A convenient mix of prawns, scallops, and fish pieces; useful for bisque-style toppings or reef-and-beef presentations. - ** Freeze in sealed bags for up to 3 months.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in omega-3 fatty acids, iodine, selenium, zinc, and B12. Oysters are particularly high in zinc. Prawns are high in cholesterol but low in saturated fat.

Seafood.purpose: Provides a lean, high-quality protein with delicate to robust flavour depending on species. Used in bistro-style presentations, sauces, toppings, stir-fries, and paired with beef in classic surf-and-turf dishes.
Seafood.storage: Storage:** Keep refrigerated and use within 1–2 days.

Sesame Seeds.notes: Common types and - **Black Sesame Seeds:** Earthier, slightly bitter; used for visual contrast, flavour, or in Asian desserts and breads. - **Usage Tips:** Toast lightly to release oils and enhance aroma. Can be added whole, crushed, or ground.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in calcium, magnesium, iron, phosphorus, and B vitamins. Contains healthy polyunsaturated and monounsaturated fats, plus antioxidants such as sesamol.

Sesame Seeds.purpose: Adds nutty flavour, crunch, texture, and visual appeal. Can be incorporated into breads, pastries, cookies, granolas, and coatings; ground forms contribute to pastes, sauces, and dressings.
Sesame Seeds.storage: Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight container to preserve freshness.
Sesame Seeds.usageTips:
usage:

- **White Sesame Seeds:** Mild, nutty flavour; ideal for sprinkling on breads, buns, and pastries, or grinding into pastes like tahini.

Snow Peas.notes: Flat, pale green pea pods with very small peas inside, harvested young before the peas develop. The entire pod is edible — crisp, sweet, and tender with a fresh, grassy flavour. Requires minimal cooking; briefly stir-fry, steam, or blanch for 1-2 minutes to retain crunch and bright colour. Overcooking makes them limp and dull. Trim the stem end and remove the string along the seam before cooking. Common in Asian stir-fries and as a crisp vegetable side. Store refrigerated and use within 3-4 days.
Snow Peas.purpose: Adds crisp texture, fresh sweetness, and vibrant green colour to stir-fries, noodle dishes, and salads. Provides visual contrast and a light, clean flavour that balances richer ingredients.

Sourdough Starter.notes: A living culture of wild yeast and lactobacilli bacteria cultivated in a mixture of flour and water. Used as the sole leavening agent in sourdough bread, replacing commercial yeast with a slower, more complex fermentation. Requires regular feeding with fresh flour and water to maintain activity. Before use, the starter should be fully risen, bubbly, and smell pleasantly sour and yeasty — not sharp or acetone-like. A stiff sweet starter (lower hydration, fed with sugar) produces a milder flavour suitable for enriched doughs like cinnamon rolls. Can be stored in the refrigerator between bakes and revived with a few feedings. Discard a portion before each feed to maintain health and volume.
Sourdough Starter.purpose: Provides natural leavening and distinctive tangy flavour to sourdough breads and enriched doughs. Creates an open crumb structure and improved keeping quality through slow fermentation.

Soy Lecithin.notes: Common usage and benefits: - **Emulsifier:** Helps blend water and fat-based ingredients in doughs, chocolate, confections, sauces, and dressings. - **Dough Conditioner:** Improves elasticity, gas retention, and crumb structure in yeast breads, rolls, and enriched doughs. - **Shelf Life:** Slows staling, moisture loss, and improves softness; promotes even browning in baked goods. - **5–2% of flour weight in bread recipes. Use sparingly, as excess may affect flavour or dough handling.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains choline (essential for liver and brain function), phosphatidylcholine, and phosphatidylinositol; naturally derived from soybeans. Minimal sugars and starch.

Soy Lecithin.purpose: Enhances dough elasticity, structure, and gas retention. Acts as an emulsifier to stabilize mixtures containing fat and water, improving texture and consistency. Extends shelf life and promotes even browning and soft crumb development in baked goods, chocolate, spreads, and sauces.
Soy Lecithin.storage: Store in a cool, dry, airtight container away from light.

Soy Sauce.notes: The standard, all-purpose soy sauce used in most cooking. Made from fermented soybeans and wheat, it is thin, salty, and amber-brown with a clean umami flavour. When a recipe simply calls for 'soy sauce' without specifying light or dark, this is what is meant. Used for seasoning, marinating, stir-frying, dipping, and as the foundational salty element in countless Asian dishes. Adds salt and savoury depth without dramatically darkening the food.
Soy Sauce.purpose: Provides the primary salty, savoury, umami foundation in Asian cooking. Used across marinades, stir-fries, dipping sauces, and braises to build depth and balance sweetness and acidity.
Soy Sauce.storage: Store in a cool, dry place; refrigerate after opening for best freshness.

Spinach.notes: Common types and - **Leaf Spinach:** Larger, slightly stronger-flavoured leaves; suitable for sautéing, baking, or adding to sauces and soups. - **Usage Tips:** Can be used fresh or frozen. Squeeze out excess water before incorporating into pastries, pies, or quiches to prevent sogginess. Pair well with eggs, cheese, cream, or garlic for enhanced flavour. - ** Use frozen spinach directly from freezer; avoid repeated thawing to preserve nutrients and texture.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: High in vitamin A, vitamin C, vitamin K1, folate, iron, calcium, and antioxidants; low in sodium and sugar.

Spinach.purpose: Adds vibrant green colour, mild flavour, and nutritional value to dishes. Provides moisture and texture in pastries, quiches, soups, and sautés. Enhances overall presentation and complements other ingredients without overpowering.
Spinach.storage: Storage:** Store fresh spinach in a cool, dry place or refrigerated in a sealed bag.
Spinach.usageTips:
usage:

- **Baby Spinach:** Tender, mild-flavoured leaves; ideal for fresh salads, smoothies, and as a filling in pastries or quiches.

Spring Onion.notes: Common types and Mild onion flavour; suitable for raw use in salads, salsas, and garnishes, or lightly cooked in stir-fries, soups, and omelettes. - **Usage Tips:** Use both white and green parts; white for mild aromatic base, green for freshness and colour. Slice thinly or chop depending on dish. Add near the end of cooking to preserve colour and aroma. - ** Use within a few days for maximum freshness. Can be frozen chopped, but texture softens.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in vitamin K, vitamin C, folate, and antioxidants; provides small amounts of calcium, iron, and potassium. Low in calories and fat.

Spring Onion.purpose: Adds fresh, mild onion flavour and bright green colour. Enhances salads, stir-fries, soups, omelettes, and garnishes without overpowering other flavours.
Spring Onion.storage: Storage:** Store unwashed in a perforated bag or wrapped in paper in the fridge.
Spring Onion.usageTips:
usage:

- **Spring Onion / Green Onion:** Long green stalk with a small, undeveloped white bulb.

Stock.notes: Common types and Homemade is preferred for control over salt and flavour; store-bought is convenient but may contain sodium and additives. - **Chicken Stock / Broth:** Light, versatile base for soups, stews, risottos, and sauces. Use homemade for deeper flavour; store-bought is suitable for convenience. - **Vegetable Stock:** Provides flavour without meat; made by simmering vegetables, herbs, and aromatics. Great for vegetarian or vegan recipes. - **Fish / Seafood Stock:** Adds umami to seafood soups, stews, and sauces; typically made from fish bones or shellfish shells. - **Usage Tips:** Stocks can be used as cooking liquids for grains, risottos, and braised dishes, or reduced for concentrated sauces. - ** Use airtight containers to preserve flavour and prevent contamination.

Strawberries.notes: Use fresh or frozen; wash gently and hull before use. Common in desserts like cakes, tarts, pavlovas, smoothies, and as toppings for breakfast dishes. Frozen strawberries are best used in cooking or baking where texture is less critical. Can be macerated with sugar or paired with citrus to enhance natural sweetness. - ** Handle gently to avoid bruising.

Strawberries.purpose: Adds natural sweetness, bright colour, aroma, and moisture. Enhances texture and flavour in desserts, pastries, and beverages. Can be used fresh or cooked depending on recipe requirements.

Sugar.notes: Common types and - **Coconut Sugar / Coconut Palm Sugar / Palm Sugar:** Made from palm sap; less sweet than white sugar with subtle caramel or smoky notes. Adjust moisture and sweetness in baking. - **Dark Brown / Muscovado / Unrefined Brown Sugar:** High molasses content adds moisture, deep caramel flavour, and dark colour. Ideal for gingerbread, rich cookies, puddings, and sauces. - **Light Brown / Soft Brown Sugar:** Contains small molasses amount; adds gentle caramel flavour and soft texture in cookies, cakes, and sauces. - **Demerara Sugar:** Large golden crystals; retain texture when baked or sprinkled on desserts. Adds crunch and subtle caramel notes. - **Icing / Confectioners’ / Powdered Sugar:** Finely powdered; dissolves instantly. Used for frostings, dusting, and smooth decorative finishes. - **Raw / Natural Raw Sugar:** Less refined, larger crystals, natural golden colour. Best for beverages, toppings, and finishing rather than precise baking. - **White / Granulated / Cane Sugar:** Standard refined sugar; provides clean sweetness, affects spread, texture, moisture retention, and browning. - **Usage Tips:** Adjust type based on texture, sweetness, and moisture impact in recipes.

Brown and unrefined sugars add deeper flavour and colour; caster and icing sugar enhance smoothness and aeration in delicate batters and frostings. Essential for desserts, breads, sauces, and beverages.

- **Caster / Superfine Sugar:** Fine crystals dissolve quickly; ideal for sponge cakes, meringues, creamed butter mixtures, and delicate batters.

Taco Seasoning.notes: **Commercial packet (Old El Paso):** Contains Corn Starch, Chili Pepper, Maltodextrin, Salt, Spice, Onion Powder — 1 packet (35 g) per 500 g mince. **Homemade blend (see tacoseasoning recipe):** 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp paprika, 1 tsp chili powder, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp onion powder, 1 tsp dried oregano, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1/2 tsp plain flour. Tia Maria.storage: Storage:** Keep in a cool, dark place; refrigerate after opening for best quality.
Tia Maria.usageTips: Commonly used in desserts such as cakes, trifles, mousses, and chocolate-based recipes.

Toblerone.notes: Triangular chunks can be chopped, melted, or folded into cakes, brownies, or desserts. Can be used as decoration, filling, or in confections. - ** Avoid high temperatures to prevent melting.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Provides small amounts of calcium, iron, magnesium, and some B vitamins from cocoa and almonds. High in sugar and fat, primarily for flavour and energy.

Toblerone.purpose: Adds chocolate, honey, and almond nougat flavour. Contributes sweetness, texture, and richness to baked goods and desserts.
Toblerone.storage: Storage:** Keep in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight.

Tomato Paste.notes: A thick, concentrated paste made from tomatoes that have been cooked down and strained to remove seeds and skins. Deep red with an intense, slightly sweet tomato flavour. Used to add depth, richness, and colour to sauces, stews, braises, and soups. A small amount goes a long way. Fry briefly in oil at the start of cooking to caramelise the sugars and deepen the flavour before adding liquids. Sold in small cans, jars, or tubes. Can be frozen in tablespoon portions for convenience.
Tomato Paste.purpose: Adds concentrated tomato flavour, deep red colour, richness, and body to sauces, stews, and braises. Caramelises in hot oil to build a deep savoury base. Essential in Italian, Filipino, and many other cuisines.
Tomato Paste.storage: Store in the refrigerator after opening — tubes keep longest.

Tomato Sauce.notes: A smooth, sweet-tangy condiment made from tomatoes, vinegar, sugar, and spices. In Australian cooking, tomato sauce is the equivalent of ketchup — used as a table condiment and as an ingredient in sauces, glazes, and marinades. Adds sweetness, acidity, and a familiar savoury tomato flavour. In recipes, it can be used to build quick sweet-sour bases for stir-fries and dipping sauces.
Tomato Sauce.purpose: Adds sweetness, tang, and tomato flavour to sauces, glazes, marinades, and as a finishing condiment. Provides the sweet-tangy base in sweet and sour sauces and Filipino-style stews.
Tomato Sauce.storage: Store in the pantry before opening; refrigerate after opening.

Tomatoes.notes: Versatile tomato varieties for curries, sauces, stews, and general cooking. Choose the form based on recipe requirements and desired texture: * **Fresh Tomatoes:** Ripe and firm; ideal for salads, salsas, and fresh sauces. * **Roma:** Meaty, low in seeds; perfect for sauces, roasting, and cooking. * **Cherry / Grape Tomatoes:** Small, sweet, firm; great for roasting, salads, or quick sautés. * **Canned Tomatoes:** Peeled, diced, or crushed; excellent for long-simmered sauces and soups. * **Tomato Puree / Passata:** Smooth, liquid consistency; perfect for soups, sauces, and gravies where a silky texture is desired. * **Tomato Paste:** Concentrated tomato flavour; often caramelised slightly to deepen taste; use in small quantities for sauces, stews, and curries. For thicker consistency, drain excess liquid from canned tomatoes if needed. Store fresh tomatoes at room temperature (refrigerate only if very ripe). Canned, pureed, or paste forms should be stored in a cool, dry place and refrigerated after opening.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in vitamin C, vitamin A (from beta-carotene), potassium, folate, and antioxidants like lycopene. Supports immunity and heart health.

Tomatoes.purpose: Adds sweetness, acidity, colour, and body to curries, sauces, soups, and stews. Provides texture, depth, and concentrated flavour depending on tomato variety and form used.

Turkish Delight.notes: Often dusted with icing sugar or desiccated coconut. Can be chopped into smaller pieces for incorporation into cakes, pastries, or served as a sweet snack.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Minimal vitamins and minerals; mainly a source of quick energy from sugar.

Turkish Delight.purpose: Adds sweet, chewy texture and flavored candy notes to desserts. Enhances visual appeal and provides bursts of sweetness in pastries, cakes, and confections.
Turkish Delight.storage: Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight container to prevent sticking and moisture absorption.

Turmeric.notes: A vibrant, golden spice prized in many cuisines for its earthy, slightly bitter flavour and warm aroma. Often combined with other spices in curries, stews, and marinades. To preserve its brilliant colour and delicate flavour, add towards the end of cooking or cook briefly. Can be used in spice blends, sauces, rice dishes, pickles, and even beverages like golden milk.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in manganese, iron, potassium, and antioxidants like curcumin; supports anti-inflammatory properties.

Turmeric.purpose: Adds warm, earthy flavour, a bright golden hue, and aromatic depth to curries, sauces, rice dishes, and spice blends.
Turmeric.storage: Store in a cool, dry place away from light to maintain colour and potency.

Ube.notes: Cook, boil, or steam before mashing. Peel before cooking if fresh. Freezes well once cooked. Can be used grated, pureed, or in powdered form. Works well combined with coconut milk or condensed milk for desserts.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: High in vitamin C, vitamin A precursors (beta-carotene), potassium, and antioxidants. Supports immune function, eye health, and gut health.

Ube.purpose: Used in desserts, pastries, ice creams, and Filipino treats. Provides a sweet, nutty flavour and vibrant purple colour. Can be incorporated into breads, cakes, puddings, and fillings.

Vanilla.notes: Forms and - **Vanilla Extract / Pure Vanilla Extract:** Alcohol-based extract made from real vanilla beans; commonly used in baking and desserts. - **Vanilla Paste:** Thick, concentrated vanilla product with seeds; combines convenience of extract with visual appeal of beans. - **Vanilla Essence / Imitation / Artificial Vanilla:** Synthetic alternative; alcohol-based; cheaper, convenient option for baking. Flavor is less complex than pure vanilla. Store all vanilla products in a cool, dark place away from strong odours. Vanilla pods may be refrigerated or frozen for extended storage.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains small amounts of calcium, magnesium, and potassium. Vanilla is primarily valued for flavour rather than nutrition.

Vanilla.purpose: Adds aromatic, sweet vanilla flavour to baked goods, creams, custards, sauces, and desserts. Enhances overall sweetness and aroma.

Veal.notes: Veal is the meat of young cattle, with a mild, delicate flavour and tender texture. - **Veal Escalopes / Schnitzel:** Thin cuts, usually from the leg, pounded flat. Cooks very quickly — 1–2 minutes per side. Ideal for crumbing, pan-frying, or topping with sauces (Cordon Bleu, Scaloppine, Oscar, Madagascar). - **Veal Medallions / Steaks:** Thicker cuts used whole; excellent for bistro-style dishes with cream or wine sauces. - **Cooking Notes:** Veal has less fat than beef so it can dry out quickly. Do not overcook — aim for just cooked through. - **Classic Bistro Pairings:** Lemon-butter, mushroom cream, Marsala, Cordon Bleu (ham and cheese filling), Oscar (crab/seafood topping).

Veal.purpose: Mild, tender protein that absorbs sauces and seasonings readily. Ideal for elegant, restaurant-style dishes where delicate texture and clean flavour are desired.

Vegemite.notes: Spread thin; strong, acquired taste. Can be used in sandwiches, on toast, in savory pastries, or to add depth to soups and sauces.

Vegemite.purpose: Adds salty, umami flavour and depth to breads, sandwiches, savory pastries, and cooked dishes. Enhances savoury notes and provides a distinctive, bold taste.
Vegemite.storage: Store in a cool, dry place and refrigerate after opening to maintain flavour and freshness.

Vermicelli Rice Noodles.notes: Soak in water before cooking; do not overcook. Ideal for stir-fries, soups, spring rolls, and salads. Can be lightly fried after soaking for added texture.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Low in fat; contains small amounts of iron and B vitamins depending on brand. Primarily a source of carbohydrates.

Vermicelli Rice Noodles.storage: Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight container to prevent moisture and clumping.

Vindaloo Paste.notes: Traditional Indian-style curry paste originating from Goa, adapted from Portuguese influences. Made from a blend of dried red chilies, garlic, ginger, vinegar, cumin, coriander, turmeric, mustard seeds, and sometimes cinnamon or cloves. Can be used directly in curries or as a marinade for meat, poultry, or vegetables. Adjust quantity to control spiciness; balance with coconut milk, yogurt, or cream if desired. Store refrigerated in an airtight container; freezes well for long-term use. Essential for creating authentic, layered, and aromatic curry dishes.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains vitamin C, iron, and antioxidants from spices; low in fat and protein; primarily contributes flavour rather than bulk nutrition.

Vindaloo Paste.purpose: Provides intense heat, bold spice, and complex aromatic flavour. Acts as both seasoning and base for curries, stews, and marinades. Enhances depth, colour, and warmth in Indian-inspired dishes. Can be used as the primary flavouring or blended with other pastes for nuanced profiles.

Vinegar.notes: Common types: - **White / Distilled Vinegar:** Strong, clear vinegar; - **Cane / Brown Vinegar:** Milder, slightly sweet; traditional in Filipino and Asian cooking. - **Apple Cider Vinegar (ACV):** Made from fermented apples; used in dressings, marinades, and vegan baking. Raw/unfiltered versions contain the “mother”. - **Other Types:** Coconut vinegar and wine vinegars add specific regional flavours. Adjust type according to recipe. Store all vinegars in a cool, dark place; most have long shelf life due to acidity.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains trace amounts of potassium, magnesium, and other minerals depending on source. Low-calorie, primarily contributes flavour rather than significant nutrients.

Vinegar.purpose: Adds acidity, tang, and balance to dishes. Can tenderise meats, enhance flavours, and activate leavening in baking.
Vinegar.usageTips: commonly used for pickling, cleaning, and baking (activates baking soda).

Vital Wheat Gluten.notes: Powdered form of wheat gluten with very high protein content (~70–80%). Commonly added to low-gluten flours (like whole wheat, rye, or spelt) to improve elasticity, structure, and rise in bread. Typically used at 1–3% of flour weight; too much can result in dense, chewy, or rubbery bread. Can also be used to make seitan (vegetarian protein) by hydrating and kneading into a meat-like texture. Mix thoroughly with flour to distribute evenly.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains small amounts of iron, magnesium, and selenium. Primarily contributes protein; low in fat and carbohydrates.

Vital Wheat Gluten.purpose: Enhances gluten development, dough elasticity, and gas retention for better volume and texture in yeast breads. Improves chewiness and structure in whole grain or gluten-weak doughs. Essential for achieving soft, airy crumb in artisan breads, rolls, bagels, and pizza bases, and forms the base for plant-based meat substitutes like seitan.
Vital Wheat Gluten.storage: Store in a cool, dry place in airtight container to prevent moisture absorption.

Walnuts.notes: Walnuts are slightly bitter, earthy nuts used in baking and cooking. - ** Toasting enhances aroma and flavor. - **Pairings:** Complements chocolate, caramel, apples, pears, cinnamon, and vanilla. - ** - **Substitutions:** Pecans can be used in place of walnuts in most recipes.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in omega-3 fatty acids, vitamin E, magnesium, and antioxidants; provides healthy fats and protein.

Walnuts.purpose: Adds crunch, earthy richness, and distinctive flavor to baked goods, desserts, and salads.
Walnuts.storage: Storage:** Store in an airtight container in a cool, dark place; refrigerate or freeze for longer shelf life.
Walnuts.usageTips: Usage:** Chop, toast, or use whole in cakes, cookies, brownies, granola, and salads.

Wine.notes: Cook alcohol off if desired to avoid harshness and enhance flavour. Ideal for sauces, braises, reductions, and marinades. Store unopened bottles in a cool, dark place; refrigerate after opening and use within a few days for best flavour.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains trace amounts of potassium and small antioxidants, especially in red wine. Mainly contributes calories from alcohol; negligible macronutrients.

Wine.purpose: Adds acidity, depth, aroma, and complexity to sauces, braises, reductions, and marinades. Enhances natural flavours of meats, vegetables, and seafood while providing subtle sweetness or dryness depending on the type of wine.
Wine.usageTips: Commonly used types include red, white, sweet, dry, and Chinese cooking wines such as Shaoxing.

Worcestershire Sauce.notes: A thin, dark brown fermented liquid condiment made from vinegar, molasses, anchovies, tamarind, and spices. Complex, savoury, and tangy with a deep umami character. Used sparingly — a few dashes add depth and complexity to meat dishes, stews, sauces, and marinades. Particularly good at enhancing beef.
Worcestershire Sauce.purpose: Adds complex savoury depth, umami, and subtle tang. Enhances the meaty flavour of beef dishes, stews, pies, and sauces. A little goes a long way.
Worcestershire Sauce.storage: Store in a cool, dry place; does not require refrigeration due to its fermented, high-acid nature.

Xanthan Gum.notes: A polysaccharide derived from bacterial fermentation of sugars, Typically added at 0.5–1% of flour weight (about 1/4–1/2 teaspoon per cup of flour). Helps bind ingredients, trap gas during rising, and improve moisture retention. Can be used in breads, muffins, cakes, and sauces as a stabilizer or thickener. Overuse can create gummy or dense texture. Dissolve in water or oil before mixing into dry ingredients for best results.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Minimal micronutrients; mainly contributes soluble fiber, which can aid digestion and improve texture in recipes.

Xanthan Gum.purpose: Provides structure, elasticity, and cohesion in gluten-free doughs and batters, allowing improved rise, crumb, and chewiness. Enhances moisture retention and prevents crumbling in baked goods. Also acts as a thickening and stabilizing agent in sauces, dressings, and gluten-free mixtures.
Xanthan Gum.storage: Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight container to prevent clumping.
Xanthan Gum.usageTips: commonly used in gluten-free baking to mimic the structure and elasticity of gluten.

Yeast.notes: Available as active dry, instant (rapid-rise), and fresh yeast. Active dry should be bloomed in warm liquid (about 38–43°C). Instant yeast can be mixed directly into dry ingredients. Fresh yeast is highly perishable but offers strong fermentation. Sensitive to heat and salt; water that is too hot will kill it. Essential for breads, pizza dough, rolls, brioche, and fermented doughs.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in B-vitamins (B1, B2, B3, B6, B9), selenium, chromium, and protein; contributes nutrients and umami flavor to baked goods.

Yeast.purpose: Ferments sugars to produce carbon dioxide and alcohol, causing dough to rise and developing flavor, structure, and aroma in baked goods.
Yeast.storage: Store in a cool, dry place; refrigerate or freeze unopened yeast for extended shelf life.

Yogurt.notes: Common types: - **Greek-Style / Thick Yogurt:** Strained for thicker texture and higher protein; adds richness and creaminess. Ideal for curries, dips, and desserts. - **Natural / Plain Yogurt:** Unflavoured, unsweetened; versatile for curries, sauces, marinades, and baking. Whisk before adding for smooth consistency. - **Flavoured Yogurt:** Sweetened or fruit-flavoured; generally used in desserts or snacks rather than cooking. Store all yogurt in the refrigerator and use by the best-before date. Greek yogurt has a longer shelf life due to straining.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in calcium, vitamin B12, riboflavin (B2), phosphorus, potassium, and probiotics. Greek-style yogurt is higher in protein and lower in carbohydrates.

Yogurt.purpose: Adds creaminess, tanginess, and moisture to curries, sauces, baked goods, marinades, and dressings. Can also help tenderise meats and balance spices.

Zucchini.notes: Best used young and firm for optimal texture. Can be eaten raw, grilled, baked, sautéed, or stuffed. Overcooking can cause excess moisture. Flowers are also edible. Store unwashed in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Good source of vitamin C, vitamin A, potassium, and antioxidants. Provides hydration due to high water content.

Zucchini.purpose: Provides mild, tender flesh that absorbs flavours well. Adds texture, moisture, and subtle sweetness to dishes.
